criteria.check: Distinguishes GET and POST after an ambiguous connection failure; intended idempotent effect is distinct from receiving a response.
Explains both 429 and 503 and covers each for GET and POST; status and Retry-After alone do not establish POST deduplication.
Explains non-negative integer seconds and HTTP-date Retry-After, using response receipt/current wall-clock time appropriately.
Handles absent/invalid Retry-After with an explicitly proposed bounded policy, preserving a valid server-indicated delay.
Pseudocode bounds attempts to at most 3 including the initial request; it does not claim the RFC prescribes this number.
Pseudocode uses a total 30-second deadline, includes request time and waits, and bounds every request timeout by remaining time.
Stops when the selected wait exceeds remaining time and rechecks the deadline before a later attempt.
Pseudocode enforces the stated GET/POST eligibility; an unavailable response is not treated as proof the POST was never applied.
Uses original RFC sources and meaningful section references; recommendations are separated from normative requirements.

Does not promise eventual success or invent an idempotency-key guarantee; acknowledges RFC 9110 9.2.2's SHOULD NOT on retrying a failed automatic retry, or makes a justified bounded policy choice rather than claiming blanket RFC approval.

scoring: Manual assessment per criterion: satisfied / partial / missing. Engine completion status is reported separately. Pseudocode is inspected, not described as executed code.
